reasoning: Both attempts are functionally correct. A calls useSignalState in app's mounted scope and leaves BlockPicker untouched as a pure Vide view. B moves the bridge into BlockPicker, so BlockPicker now depends on Charm and its `Selected` prop must be a Charm getter, which goes against criterion 5.

criteria.criterion: BlockPlacer owns selection as Charm signal
criteria.note: `local getBlockType, setSelectedName = Charm.signal(...)`; only the getter is exported, and `setBlockType` keeps the `assert(BlockTypes.ByName[name])` before calling `setSelectedName`.

criteria.criterion: Hotbar bridges via useSignalState in mounted scope
criteria.note: `VideCharm.useSignalState(BlockPlacer.getBlockType)` is called in the body of `app`, which runs inside `mount`, so the source is tracked and disposed with the UI.

criteria.criterion: Single copy of selection, BlockTypeChanged removed
criteria.note: The mirrored `source` and its event connection are deleted, the BindableEvent is gone, and `placeAt` reads `getBlockType()`.
`Charm.listen(BlockPlacer.getBlockType, applyBlockType)` colors the ghost right away and again on every change.

criteria.criterion: BlockPicker unchanged / view fed by caller
criteria.note: BlockPicker is untouched and still gets a Vide source as `Selected` from its caller.
The change is minimal and typed, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua all pass.

criteria.criterion: BlockPlacer owns selection as Charm signal
criteria.note: `getSelected, setSelected = Charm.signal(...)`; the getter is exported as `() -> string`, and `setBlockType` keeps the assert.

criteria.criterion: Hotbar bridges via useSignalState in mounted scope
criteria.note: `useSignalState(props.Selected)` is called in the BlockPicker body, which still runs inside mount, so it works; but Main passes the raw Charm getter as `Selected`.

criteria.criterion: Single copy of selection, BlockTypeChanged removed
criteria.note: The mirror source and the BindableEvent are removed, and `placeAt` uses `getSelected()`.

criteria.criterion: BlockPicker unchanged / view fed by caller
criteria.note: BlockPicker now requires VideCharm and expects `Selected` to be a Charm getter; a caller passing a Vide source would get an outline that never updates.
Works and passes all checks, but makes an unneeded change to BlockPicker.

strengths: Bridge sits at the composition root in `app`, inside the mount scope
BlockPicker stays a pure Vide view with no changes
weaknesses: The getter is exported without an explicit type annotation (minor)

strengths: Clear comments and an explicit getter type
weaknesses: BlockPicker is now tied to Charm, so its props expect a Charm getter
